title: Graph Systems of Linear Equations
student_objective: I can graph two linear equations, identify their intersection, and classify the system as one solution, no solution, or infinitely many solutions.

concept_cards.title: The solution is the intersection
concept_cards.content: A point that lies on both lines makes both equations true. That shared point is the solution of the system.

concept_cards.title: One solution
concept_cards.content: If two different lines cross once, the system has exactly one solution.

concept_cards.title: No solution
concept_cards.content: Parallel lines have the same slope and different intercepts, so they never meet.

concept_cards.title: Infinitely many solutions
concept_cards.content: If the equations graph as the same line, every point on the line satisfies both equations.

intersection.teacher_signal: Student reads a point from only one line.

parallel.teacher_signal: Student expects parallel lines to intersect.

same-line.teacher_signal: Student treats coincident lines as one solution.

items.prompt: If two different lines intersect at (2,3), what is the system's solution?
items.tutor_behavior: Connect the crossing point to the ordered-pair solution.
hint_steps: The solution must lie on both lines.
The shared point is their intersection.

solution_steps.explanation: The point lies on both lines.
That shared point solves the system.

items.prompt: What kind of solution does a system have if the two lines are parallel and distinct?
items.tutor_behavior: Relate parallel lines to absence of intersection.
hint_steps: A graphical solution requires an intersection.

items.prompt: The graphs of y=x+1 and y=-x+5 intersect at (2,3). State the solution.
items.tutor_behavior: Model reading the intersection directly from the graph.

items.prompt: Classify the system y=2x+1 and y=2x-4.
items.tutor_behavior: Compare slopes and intercepts before graphing.
hint_steps: They are parallel, so no solution.

solution_steps.explanation: Distinct parallel lines do not intersect.

items.prompt: The lines y=x+2 and y=-2x+8 intersect at (2,4). What is the solution?
items.tutor_behavior: Read and state the ordered pair.
hint_steps: Find the point on both lines.

solution_steps.explanation: The point is shared by both graphs.

items.tutor_behavior: Use equal slopes and different intercepts.
hint_steps: The lines are parallel, so no solution.

items.tutor_behavior: Rewrite the second equation before classifying.
hint_steps: Both equations are the same line, so infinitely many solutions.

solution_steps.explanation: Every point on the line is shared.

items.prompt: A graph shows two lines crossing at (-1,5). State the solution.
items.tutor_behavior: Student reads a graphical solution independently.
hint_steps: The crossing point is the shared point.

solution_steps.explanation: This point lies on both lines.

hint_steps: Parallel distinct lines give no solution.

items.tutor_behavior: Rewrite standard form to compare equations.
hint_steps: Both equations are identical, so infinitely many solutions.

items.prompt: The lines in a system intersect at (4,-2). What is the solution?
items.tutor_behavior: Mastery check on reading the intersection.
hint_steps: A system solution is the shared point.

solution_steps.explanation: The point lies on both lines.

hint_steps: Same line means infinitely many solutions.

items.prompt: How many solutions does a system have when two nonparallel lines cross once?
items.tutor_behavior: Connect graph shape to solution count.
hint_steps: Each intersection is a shared solution.

items.prompt: What graphical feature identifies the solution of a system of two linear equations?
hint_steps: The solution must satisfy both equations.
On a graph, it lies on both lines.
